description:
Shimen Niudi Cha is a green tea from Shimen County in northern Hunan, named in lists of the province's famous greens alongside teas such as Guzhang Maojian and Gaoqiao Yinfeng. Beyond those listings, very little is written about it.

Nothing specific is published about how it is made, so the safe assumption is the ordinary path of a green tea: heat to stop oxidation, then shaping and drying.

The same goes for taste. Hunan's spring greens are typically fresh and fragrant, and it is fair to start there, but that is what is typical of the class and not a description of this tea. Brew with cooler water and short steeps until you learn the leaf.

If you come across it, ask the seller about the village and the picking date. It would be an uncommon find, and anything they can tell you first-hand is worth more than a label. Shimen Yinfeng is the better-known green tea from the same county if you want a comparison.
history: Little is documented. The tea appears in overviews of Hunan's named teas as a Shimen green, but when it began, who made it known and how it has changed are not on record.
